messages:
samira: Heads up — after yesterday's RBAC cleanup I'm seeing a flood of SAML failures + SCIM deprovision spikes for a subset of users. Posting correlation graphs in a sec. @oncall-sre ?

jordan: I can see the same. Audit shows a bunch of SCIM 409/404s and SAML assertions rejected with nameid mismatch around 2024-11-18T03:12:xxZ. Also a KMS error repeated in the provisioning service logs.

liam: do we have the KMS alias rotation notes handy? we rotated a couple aliases last night for the prod KMS key.

samira: We rotated alias but followed runbook. Confirmed we updated control-plane secret in vault, but private deploys might still reference old alias.

jordan: Paste from provisioning-service log (redacted):
```
2024-11-18T03:12:17.482Z ERROR provisioning-service: KMSUnwrapFailed keyAlias=redwood-kms-prod-v2 err="failed to unwrap: context-mismatch"
2024-11-18T03:12:17.483Z WARN scim-sync: user=alice@acme.com externalId=urn:acme:user:alice action=deprovision status=409
2024-11-18T03:12:18.001Z ERROR saml-processor: Assertion rejected reason="NameID truncated" subject=alice@acme.com
```

oncall-sre: That context-mismatch KMS error smells like the decryption context used at encrypt time differs from decrypt time — maybe a change in service principal or additional context field added during RBAC cleanup.

liam: I dug through the commit that rolled the RBAC changes — we added a new principal and also changed the provisioning service to add `org_id` into the KMS encryption context for SCIM tokens. If someone rolled the alias without updating all services that would cause unwrap failures.

samira: bingo. The truncated NameID is an independent downstream symptom: because the provisioner couldn't decrypt cached extId, it fell back to creating a new externalId which got truncated by the SAML NameID length check -> mismatch with IdP -> IdP rejects assertion -> user gets deprovisioned locally -> loop.

sec-bot: [alert] provisioning-service retry queue > 200 for tenant acme-corp :incidents:

jordan: mitigation plan: 1) pause SCIM sync for affected org(s), 2) rollback KMS alias to previous alias (redwood-kms-prod-v1) to let pending decrypts succeed, 3) run extid backfill for users that got a bad externalId, 4) re-enable once validated. Thoughts?

liam: Agree. Also capture full audit trail for the alias rotation and RBAC commit — we need to show who/what changed the encryption context. Open a vuln-triage ticket to track root cause and potential escalation.

samira: I'm pausing SCIM for acme-corp now (api: POST /admin/orgs/acme/pause-scim -> 200). Pausing gives us breathing room.

samira: Rolling alias back to redwood-kms-prod-v1 and restoring previous secret in vault for provisioning-service. Running quick smoke.

jordan: smoke logs: 
```
2024-11-18T03:22:33.110Z INFO kms: alias redwood-kms-prod-v1 set on provisioning-service
2024-11-18T03:22:33.211Z INFO provisioning-service: KMS unwrap succeeded for user=alice@acme.com
2024-11-18T03:22:33.212Z INFO scim-sync: queued backfill for alice@acme.com status=queued
```

liam: Starting backfill script: `/ops/scripts/backfill_extid.sh --org acme-corp --since 2024-11-17T00:00Z`

sec-bot: [info] SCIM queue drained to <50 items for acme-corp

oncall-sre: Confirming SAML assertions are now accepted for a sample user (alice) — login OK. Will keep SCIM paused until backfill completes and we verify audit logs.

samira: Opening vuln-triage ticket: VULN-2024-089 - KMS context drift after RBAC change. Adding action items: autorun tests for KMS context invariants, update runbook to validate all services reference new alias, and gating alias rotation with a small canary.

jordan: Nice. Postmortem notes: short-term fix = rollback alias + backfill. Long-term = stronger validation + telemetry on KMS unwrap reasons (context mismatch) surfaced in Console.

liam: I'll follow up with a small patch that makes the provisioning service fall back more gracefully when extId decrypt fails (emit metric + don't auto-deprovision).

samira: Thanks all. Re-opening SCIM only after backfill completes and we have green end-to-end tests.

sec-bot: [resolved] incident acme-scim-kms-20241118 at 2024-11-18T03:56:39Z — mitigation applied, monitoring in recovery.
